name: The Citadel Breach
subject: Cybersecurity
description: Defend a fortress city from increasingly sophisticated attacks. Each security concept is a defense you build or a threat you counter. You'll analyze attack vectors, architect layered defenses, implement access controls, respond to active incidents, and navigate the political landscape of governance and compliance -- all while the Citadel's enemies probe for weaknesses.

companions.name: Vex
companions.personality: Sharp, sardonic rogue who learned security by breaking it first and knows every trick in the book
companions.speech_pattern: Street-smart, cuts through jargon with blunt translations, dark humor, occasionally drops uncomfortable truths about how attackers actually think

companions.name: Dorn Ashwalker
companions.personality: Stoic dwarf paladin who treats security as a sacred duty and has zero tolerance for shortcuts
companions.speech_pattern: Blunt, military precision, no wasted words, speaks in directives and checklists, every sentence has a purpose

companions.name: The Archivist
companions.personality: Mysterious hooded figure who has seen every breach in the Citadel's history and teaches through pattern recognition
companions.speech_pattern: Cryptic but precise, answers questions with better questions, occasionally reveals a critical insight wrapped in a riddle

domains.name: General Security Concepts
concepts: Security control categories (technical, managerial, operational) and types (preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, compensating)
CIA triad (confidentiality, integrity, availability) and non-repudiation
Cryptography fundamentals (symmetric vs asymmetric, hashing, salting, key exchange)
PKI concepts (certificates, certificate authorities, CRL, OCSP, certificate pinning)
Authentication methods (MFA, passwordless, biometrics, tokens, RADIUS, TACACS+, Kerberos)
Gap analysis and security assessment concepts
Zero trust principles (never trust, always verify, microsegmentation, least privilege)
domains.mastery_signal: Can explain why a given security control is preventive vs detective, walk through a TLS handshake step by step, and design an authentication scheme that balances security with usability for a real org

domains.name: Threats, Vulnerabilities & Mitigations
concepts: Threat actor types (nation-state, insider, hacktivist, organized crime) and motivations
Malware types (ransomware, trojans, rootkits, fileless malware, logic bombs, RATs)
Social engineering attacks (phishing, spear phishing, whaling, vishing, smishing, pretexting, watering hole)
Application attacks (SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, buffer overflow, directory traversal, race conditions)
Network attacks (MITM, ARP poisoning, DNS attacks, DDoS, credential replay, on-path attacks)
Vulnerability scanning and assessment (CVE, CVSS scoring, false positives, authenticated vs unauthenticated scans)
Threat intelligence sources (OSINT, dark web, threat feeds, STIX/TAXII, IoC analysis)
Mitigation techniques (patching, segmentation, input validation, ACLs, application allow-listing)
domains.mastery_signal: Can read a vulnerability scan report, prioritize findings by CVSS score and business context, identify which are false positives, and recommend specific mitigations — not just 'patch it' but the full remediation plan with compensating controls if patching isn't immediate

domains.name: Security Architecture
concepts: Cloud security (shared responsibility model, CASB, cloud-native controls, serverless security)
Network segmentation (VLANs, DMZ, air gaps, microsegmentation, east-west traffic control)
Zero trust architecture implementation (SDP, identity-aware proxies, continuous verification)
Infrastructure security (embedded systems, SCADA/ICS, IoT hardening, firmware security)
Data protection (classification, DLP, encryption at rest and in transit, tokenization, masking)
Resilience and redundancy (load balancing, clustering, geographic dispersal, backups, RAID)
Secure application development (SDLC, DevSecOps, code signing, sandboxing, containerization)
Physical security integration (surveillance, access control vestibules, environmental controls)
domains.mastery_signal: Can design a network architecture with proper segmentation, DMZ, and zero trust principles — then explain the shared responsibility model for each cloud service type and where the org's security obligations begin and end

domains.name: Security Operations
concepts: Identity and access management (provisioning, deprovisioning, RBAC, ABAC, privilege escalation prevention)
Incident response process (preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned)
Log monitoring and SIEM (log aggregation, correlation rules, alerting, dashboards, retention policies)
Endpoint security (EDR, XDR, antivirus, host-based firewalls, DLP agents, application control)
Hardening techniques (benchmarks, CIS baselines, unnecessary services, default credentials, group policy)
Digital forensics (chain of custody, order of volatility, imaging, evidence preservation, legal hold)
Vulnerability management lifecycle (discover, assess, prioritize, remediate, verify, report)
Automation and orchestration (SOAR, scripting for security tasks, playbooks, runbooks)
domains.mastery_signal: Can walk through an incident response from first alert to lessons-learned report, explain what to collect and in what order for forensics, configure SIEM correlation rules that actually reduce noise, and write a hardening checklist for a new server deployment

domains.name: Security Program Management
concepts: Governance frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, COBIT, SOC 2)
Risk management (risk assessment, risk register, risk appetite, quantitative vs qualitative analysis, risk treatment options)
Compliance requirements (PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, SOX, FERPA, CCPA) and audit types
Data privacy concepts (data ownership, data classification, data retention, right to be forgotten, privacy impact assessment)
Security awareness training (phishing simulations, role-based training, metrics, social engineering testing)
Third-party risk management (vendor assessments, supply chain security, SLA review, right-to-audit clauses)
Business impact analysis (critical systems, MTTR, MTBF, RPO, RTO, single points of failure)
Security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines — and the difference between them
domains.mastery_signal: Can build a risk register from a business impact analysis, map controls to a governance framework, explain the difference between a policy and a procedure without hand-waving, and design a security awareness program that actually changes behavior instead of just checking a compliance box

real_world_application: Identify threats, implement security controls, respond to incidents, and manage security programs in enterprise environments
